business.title: Task interruptions in STEM online courses: understanding the mechanisms of their impact on learning outcomes and user experience
business.desc: STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) online education is increasingly characterized by high cognitive demands and complex interactive environments, which makes task interruptions a critical factor influencing both learning outcomes and user experience. This study examines the mechanisms of task interruptions in STEM online learning. We first used grounded theory to build a theoretical framework based on the Stressor-Strain-Outcome (SSO) model. Then, we conducted empirical tests using structural equation modeling (SEM) and moderation analysis. The findings indicate that: (1) task interruptions significantly increase recovery costs and cognitive and emotional strain; (2) both factors have a substantial influence on learning outcomes and user experience, with cognitive and emotional strain playing a more prominent role; and (3) active control capabilities significantly mitigate the negative effects of interruptions on cognitive and emotional processes. These results extend the applicability of the SSO framework to the context of STEM online courses and provide empirical insights into the complex mechanisms by which task interruptions impair learning effectiveness and user engagement.

technology.title: Hybrid nanowire metamaterials with ultra-wideband epsilon-near-zero mode tuning for nanophotonic applications
technology.desc: This work investigates the linear and nonlinear optical properties and guided wave modes of hybrid nanowire metamaterials (HNW-MMs), focusing on controlling their transmission characteristics. The epsilon-near-zero and hyperbolic responses of such structures are analyzed using effective medium theory, dispersion relations, and the FDTD method, under irradiation with transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) beams. Our study reveals that including silicon cores within the nanowires significantly enhances the tunability of the optical response of the metamaterial, with the emergence of additional modes at higher wavelengths. Unlike conventional nanowire MMs, these hybrid structures exhibit extra guided modes that are unique to their configuration and physical structure. The results demonstrate that by adjusting the filling ratios, the new modes can be fully controlled from the visible to the infrared (IR) range. In specific configurations, one of the new modes can achieve epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) characteristics. This work introduces a novel platform that combines controllable modes with ENZ behavior, enabling advanced functionalities not achievable in traditional metamaterial designs. Using this tunability and ENZ properties as a novel approach, a band-stop adjustable optical filter within the ENZ bandwidth is designed and simulated. Furthermore, the Kerr nonlinear effect in ENZ mode is investigated, and highly efficient all-optical nonlinear switches and relays at the nanoscale are presented.

technology.title: Ultra-compact plasma photocathode in a hybrid wakefield accelerator
technology.desc: Plasma-based particle accelerators, realized by driving plasma waves with either an intense laser pulse or particle beam, offer accelerating fields orders of magnitude higher than conventional accelerators. This enables sources of highly relativistic electron beams with significantly reduced spatial and economic footprints. However, optimizing beam quality and brightness remains the key challenge for demanding applications such as free-electron lasers. The plasma photocathode is a method for generating high-quality beams directly within plasma waves - but hitherto was exclusively realizable using the high-current drive beams from the kilometer-scale conventional accelerator at SLAC. Here we show implementation of a plasma photocathode in a millimeter-scale, purely plasma-based hybrid wakefield accelerator, powered by a 150 TW laser system. Its operation at high plasma densities enables exploitation of micrometer-scale source sizes and rapid acceleration through high-field gradients, which increases the potential output beam quality substantially. This high-density plasma photocathode can be implemented at state-of-the-art laser-plasma accelerators worldwide, and opens the door for high-quality beam production. The two-stage hybrid plasma accelerator combines laser- and particle-driven acceleration to realize a compact source of relativistic electron bunches. Here, the authors demonstrate the implementation of plasma photocathode injection in such a hybrid platform, establishing a route toward the generation of low-emittance electron beams.
